chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Children are a fragrant blossom (basil), and my two fragrant blossoms are Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn.

key_terms.الحَسَنُ: Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him), the elder grandson of the Prophet.
key_terms.الحُسَيْنُ: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), the younger grandson of the Prophet.
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah, referring to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).
key_terms.رِيحانَةٌ: A fragrant plant or herb, metaphorically used for something sweet, delightful, and cherished.

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet mean when he calls Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn his 'basil' or 'fragrant blossom'?
ai.summary: In this well-known hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) uses the metaphor of 'rihanah' (a fragrant herb like basil or mint) to denote the sweetness and spiritual delight of children, specifically elevating his grandsons, Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn, as his personal 'rihanah'. This designation underscores their unique status in Shia tradition as the pinnacle of the Ahl al-Bayt's affection and purity, linking their physical presence to spiritual fragrance. The narration highlights the deep emotional bond between the Prophet and the Imams, reinforcing their role as the beloved progeny through whom divine love is manifested.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-8 According to the same documentation, God’s Prophet (S) said, “
Children are like basil. And Al-Hassan and Al-Husayn are my basil.”
